failure_summary.description: Calls omitted, misgrouped, or misrepresented schema fields and constraints, including selectors, filters, locales, pagination, and canonical values.
Some trajectories used an adjacent endpoint, added redundant or unrequested calls, or failed to apply a documented target filter.
A requested operation was omitted when one trajectory described a computation rather than supplying code, and another requested product facet was left uncovered.

patch.reasoning: Most schema and minimality failures are already covered by the skill, so the edits clarify how to apply those rules to competing providers and selectors, and address the uncovered case of executable computations described in natural language.

edits.target: - **Scope and bundle calls appropriately.** Make separate calls for distinct targets, checks, or purposes when they require distinct arguments. Combine multiple filters or categories in one call when they concern the same operation and the endpoint supports that syntax. Do not repeat a check, add overlapping searches, or introduce unrequested calls.
edits.content: Before using multiple providers for the same subject, identify the distinct requested result each call adds; use another provider only for a separate requested facet or when the chosen provider cannot satisfy the request. If a documented filter can directly target the requested entity or location, apply it instead of making an unfiltered discovery call. A broad or comprehensive request does not authorize calls to unrequested platforms.

edits.target: Before treating a requested facet as unsupported because no dedicated endpoint exists, check whether a documented configurable endpoint can perform it through an operation or function selector.
edits.content: When the request explicitly identifies a selector dimension supported by the schema (for example, searching by group name rather than members), pass the matching documented token even if it is also the default. Do not infer a selector merely from naming an entity.

## Computation and code-execution requests

When a requested deliverable is a computation and a listed code-execution endpoint accepts source code, turn the described formula, entities, and specified assumptions into minimal runnable code; do not omit the call solely because the user described the code rather than pasting it. Use only supplied inputs or unambiguous standard constants and values. If essential nonstandard inputs are missing, do not fabricate them.
